analysis.title: US Midterms / Apple / Dovish RBA Hike / PBoC / Oil
key_insights: Focaldata's James Kanagasooriam says the view that Democrats lead generic polling by double digits looks overstated. He expects Democrats to take the House comfortably and calls the Senate effectively a toss-up, partly because Democrats must defend seats in Michigan, Minnesota and New Hampshire.

UBS Rates Sales sees a Republican sweep as the tail risk for US rates. Markets are positioned for divided government, so a sweep that raises government spending could sell off the long end. The preferred expression is a 3m USD payer switch, owning 30y payer exposure relative to 5y.
UBS Rates Trading says a December Fed hike remains the base case, while a more patient 2027 path favours H7/H8 steepeners. QRA and election risks keep long-end supply and fiscal concerns elevated.

Apple (AAPL) fell 0.24% against 3.9% implied volatility after a Q4 beat. iPhone and Mac were above expectations, iPad and Wearables below, and softer China sales put the focus on guidance. The desk read the reaction as slightly underwhelming given the iPhone launch.

The RBA hiked the cash rate 25bp to 4.85% as expected, with a 6-3 vote. UBS Economics reads dropping the tightening bias and the vote split as clearly dovish, and still expects the RBA to hold from here.

The PBoC will raise the FX reserve requirement ratio by 2ppts, from 9% to 11%, to slow CNY appreciation by reducing onshore USD liquidity. The yuan fix was 6.7150 against an estimate of 6.6517, which the desk sees as limited evidence of a major FX policy shift. The desk saw net USDCNH buying through eFX led by hedge funds, likely an unwind of bullish CNH positions.

UBS Specialist Sales says financing concerns for AI spending are building while Street 2027 capex estimates still look too low. Buyside 2027 capex figures are Meta $250bn, Alphabet $375bn and Amazon $350bn. ROI is improving but the monetization debate is unresolved, the Alphabet search bear case has resurfaced, and core cloud modestly underwhelmed on capacity constraints.

UBS Specialist Sales ranks the Mag 7 after earnings as MSFT > AMZN > NVDA > META > AAPL > GOOGL. About 20% of the S&P 500 reports this week, including BKNG, UBER, APP, EXPE, U, FWONK, ABNB, LYV and TTD.

US index and single-name implied volatility repriced higher, with VIX and VIXEQ at their highest closes since July. Skew rose sharply, suggesting clients hedged quickly. The midterms price the largest one-day SPX breakeven move through year-end at just over 1%.

South Korea October headline CPI eased to 2.8% y/y from 2.9% in September. Petroleum prices rose 14.9% and added 0.56pp, while farm prices fell 1.7%. Core CPI was 2.8%, and the finance ministry estimates fuel price caps cut headline inflation by 0.8pp.

UBS Rates Derivatives Trading sees asymmetric paid 1y1y views in AUDNZD as attractive on rising inflation expectations. The ACGB belly screens cheap, favouring long c5y ACGB MMS flies, and receiving c5y5y AUDUSD looks attractive. New Zealand duration looks stretched.

UBS keeps USDSEK and EURSEK shorts despite sharp SEK strengthening. The Riksbank decision in early November (a 25bp hike is the UBS and median estimate) and October CPIF are the near-term catalysts. UBS Economics expects a December skip and another hike in Q1 2027, taking the policy rate to 2.25%.

UBS Rates Sales recommends long UNEDIC 3.25% May-32, outright or against OAT 0% May-32, at 16bp over OATs targeting 10bp. The case rests on the state guarantee, wide spreads, strong carry and social-bond demand.

UBS Rates Trading says the UK budget was uneventful and curves steepened. Markets expect the BoE to hike 25bp to 4.0%, and a hawkish surprise could sell off December contracts. It favours front-end flatteners, long-end steepeners and 7-10y asset swap longs.

UBS Wealth Management CIO expects Brent near $110 at year-end, then $90 by June 2027 as Strait of Hormuz traffic recovers. Diplomacy may reduce some risk premium, but inventories have fallen sharply, strategic reserve releases are largely complete, and recovering Chinese imports remove a buffer.

UBS FX Options Trading says the midterm risk premium has largely faded, with FX options pricing only 25-30bp of event gap risk, below a typical NFP or CPI. The desk prefers GBPUSD and USDCHF gamma as long-vol trades after heavy supply pushed pricing lower. It sees less appeal in shorting AUDUSD and USDJPY vols, which are already low.

Crude rose 0.5% in Asia after the prior session's sharp selloff on reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island. US officials called the recent strikes defensive, and Iran's president said the supreme leader gave his government more authority to pursue peace talks.

US stocks ended near session lows as the AI trade reversed early gains, with SOX down 3.4% and US memory down 5.1%. The fade was attributed to Meta and Alphabet planning billions of dollars in bond issuance. The equal-weight S&P outperformed the cap-weighted index by 120bp.

Treasuries pared early gains on the issuance slate. The 30y ended 2bp richer and the 5s30s curve finished marginally flatter against overnight levels. Refunding estimates were roughly in line, and the small Q4 reduction flattened 5s30s slightly.

UBS FX Trading says gold's drop toward $3,875 appears to have cleared downside positioning, leaving the market neutral to slightly short. It sees resistance near $3,970-$3,975 and advises waiting for midterm results before taking new directional exposure.
